newsitem.title: UK: PRESS DIGEST - British business press - July 15.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - British business press - July 15.

text.p: This daily press summary is produced for Reuters by the Broadcast Monitoring Company, which is responsible for its contents. DAILY TELEGRAPH
-- SOFTWARE DIRECTOR DEPARTS

Troubled Internet software company Display.IT has confirmed that one of its directors, Bill Murphy, resigned last week without any public announcement. Shares in the company have slumped from 810p to 145p in the last six months, although they recovered 120p to 265p on Monday following an upbeat statement from the company which promised the release of annual results on August 15.
-- CWS JOINS HIGH STREET LOYALTY WAR

The Co-operative Wholesale Society is set to expand its discount vouchers scheme - which has been trialled in Scotland and Northern Ireland - to the rest of Britain. Under the scheme, customers receive vouchers worth 5 per cent of their purchases when they buy own-brand goods.
-- MERRILL WEIGHT BEHIND NEWS

Broker Merrill Lynch has upgraded its appraisal of shares in satellite broadcaster BSkyB from 'neutral' to 'buy'. Last November Merrill issued a News Corp bond exchangeable into BSkyB shares at 656p, but investors in the bond have been incensed by the performance of Sky shares, which were 547p when the issue was priced. On Monday, Sky shares closed at 455p, a gain of 9p on the day.
THE TIMES
-- STANDARD LIFE HITS SNAG AFTER BUDGET CHANGE TO DIVIDEND TAX

UK life insurer Standard Life has warned customers that applications to withdraw money from any of the 400 final salary schemes it operates on behalf of corporations can expect delays in receiving a quotation. The mutual is not quoting transfer values for the occupational pension funds following changes to dividend tax relief announced in the Budget.
-- MAN UTD CHIEF NETS 5.9M STG

Martin Edwards, chief executive of publicly-listed soccer club Manchester United, has netted almost 32m stg over the last 15 months from the sale of shares in the club. On Monday Edwards and his family made 5.9m stg from the sale of 910,000 shares after United's brokers, Merrill Lynch, told him of strong institutional demand for shares.
-- SIB 'NEEDS STRONGER POWERS'

Rosalind Wright, new director of the Serious Fraud Office, has called on the Treasury to conduct a radical review of the legal framework of the Securities and Investments Board when the watchdog takes on an expanded role in City regulation. The SIB is due to replace the present regime of a number of self- regulatory organisations next year.
THE GUARDIAN -- RENEGADE BUILDING SOCIETIES ARE CONVERTED INTO BAD DEALS

A survey from the Consumers' Association claims that building societies that remain mutual offer better deals on savings and mortgages than those that have converted to banks. According to the research, converting societies last year charged an average 0.31 per cent more on mortgages than their mutually-owned rivals, and 0.39 per cent more on savings.
-- RETAILERS TELL BANK TO HOLD FIRE ON ANOTHER RATE RISE

The latest snapshot of UK retail spending, compiled by the British Retail Consortium, shows that prices in shops and stores rose by just 1 per cent over the year to June. The figures have fuelled calls from retailers for the Bank of England to take a 'wait and see' approach over further interest rate rises. Separately, figures released by the Office of National Statistics show that the cost of raw materials fell by 0.8 per cent in June.
-- THORN SNAGS ON STRONG POUND

Shares in rental group Thorn fell 18.5p to 158.5p on Monday following a stormy annual general meeting. Outgoing chairman Sir Colin Southgate, the main target of shareholder anger, told the meeting that profits this year would be reduced by about 11m stg due to the strength of the pound. Shareholders in the group are still smarting from last year's demerger with EMI, which has led to more than 2.3bn stg being wiped off the combined value of the two businesses.
THE INDEPENDENT
-- ICI SHARES RISE ON $3BN DUPONT DEAL

ICI has announced the sale of half its commodity chemical business to US chemical group Du Pont for $3bn (1.8bn stg). Shares in the UK group leapt 9 per cent to 886p on news of the sale, whose price was far in excess of stock market expectations. In the two months since it acquired Unilever's speciality chemicals business for 5bn stg, ICI has now raised some 2.9bn stg from disposals, and could realise a further 1bn stg from the sale of the remaining industrial chemical assets.
-- DBS CONFIRMS ACTION BY PIA

DBS Management, a network of personal financial advisers, has confirmed that its DBS Financial Management subsidiary - which is reported to be facing a 500,000 stg fine for its part in the pensions misselling scandal - is the subject of disciplinary action from the Personal Investment Authority (PIA). However, DBS, whose chairman Ken Davy sits on the PIA board, also claimed that the newspaper report detailing the fine was based on information obtained in breach of confidence from the PIA.
-- BRENT WALKER THREATENS TO SUE GRANDMET

Leisure group Brent Walker is considering a new legal challenge to Grand Metropolitan over a long-running dispute concerning betting chain William Hill. The row dates from the acquisition by Brent Walker in 1989 of William Hill from GrandMet. Should the action go ahead, GrandMet could face a legal claim of 100m stg, posing a question mark over the group's planned 24bn stg merger with Guinness.
